name: review-document
short: Turns review findings you already have into one short Markdown write-up: verdict first, each finding ranked with evidence and a fix.
what: The skill organises a code, design or QA review into a document the reader can act on. It starts with a verdict (approve, approve with changes, request changes or blocked), ranks findings as blocking, should fix or nit, and gives each one a location, evidence and the smallest fix. It ends with what you checked and what you didn't, then lints the page with the Comark linter.
who: People who write reviews or audits for someone else to act on. It doesn't find problems for you. It only writes up findings you already have.
needs: A coding agent that supports skills
Vite+ (`vp`) or pnpm, for the install and the lint step

steps.title: Add the skills
steps.text: This is the README's install command for the repo's agent skills. It names the `comark-ui` skill, so check that review-document is in the list it offers. Without Vite+, `pnpm dlx` takes the same arguments.

steps.title: Give it your findings
steps.text: Ask your agent to write up the review. It picks a verdict, merges findings with one cause and ranks them blocking first.

steps.title: Lint the result
steps.text: The skill runs this and fixes problems until there are none. Then read the rendered page once as the reader would.
steps.code: vp dlx --package comark-linter --package comark-ui comark-lint review.md

try.label: A first prompt
try.text: "Write up the findings from this code review as a review document."

watch: It organises findings. The review itself is still your job.
The output uses Comark blocks such as `::diff` and `::tests`, so it renders best where Comark UI is set up.
The README's only skill install command names the `comark-ui` skill, not review-document.
